caption: My hair costs more than my data. Does the hustle count if it pays for itself?

slides.title:
How I spend
my R7 400
p/m stipend
South Africa
Living in Mamelodi
slides.body:
Female, 22
Single, lives with her gogo
Job: Cashier at a Spar (youth programme) + weekend braiding
Net income: R7 400 p/m

slides.title: Black tax
slides.includes: My mom's rent in Limpopo, my little brother's school shoes
slides.body: It's one fifth of what I make. I send it first so I can't talk myself out of it.

slides.title: Taxi fare
slides.includes: Two taxis each way, six days a week
slides.body: The second taxi costs more than the first and goes half the distance. I've checked.

slides.title: Groceries
slides.includes: My share of gogo's shopping, plus my own lunches
slides.body: Gogo says I eat like I'm paying for the whole house. I'm paying for a third of it.

slides.title: Data & airtime
slides.includes: Monthly bundle, top-ups when it runs out on the 20th
slides.body: Braiding bookings come in on WhatsApp, so this one is basically a work expense.

slides.title: Hair, nails & lashes
slides.includes: Mine, mostly. A client's hair is advertising
slides.body: I braid people for R350 and then spend R620 on myself. I know.

slides.title: Everything else
slides.includes: Funeral policy, stokvel, clothing account, toiletries, work shoes
slides.body: The stokvel is R300 and pays out in December. Everything else in this slide is small and constant.

slides.title: What's left
slides.body: Out of R7 400. About R20 a day, and the braiding money is what makes the month balance.

slides.title: I stopped guessing
slides.body:
I uploaded my statement to Beyond Horizon and it split my braiding money from my Spar salary.

The hair spend was the line I'd been dodging.

No bank login needed.
